Use the dial to aim; Precision enables 0.01° steps, with − and + buttons to move one step at a time. Dragging the table always moves the camera, except when placing a ball or calling a shot. The camera button opens Close, Wide, Top and Free views. Pinch to zoom; two fingers pan. Tap outside the effects panel to close it without changing your shot. Set power, then shoot. Confirm placement before shooting. To call a shot, tap the ball then the pocket; in bank pool, add the cushions in order.
Touch both object balls to score. Contact the red first on the opening shot. In marked corner areas, an object ball must leave on the second successive carom. Target: 10.
Touch both other balls, with at least one cushion before the second object ball. First to 10 points.
Touch both other balls, with at least three cushions before the second object ball. First to 10 points.

Score a carom while respecting both the rectangles and their small anchor areas. In 47/1, an object ball must leave a shared area on every shot; in 47/2 and 71/2, by the second. Leaving and returning is allowed. Target: 10.

Hit the opponent cue ball first. Outer pins: 2; centre: 4, or 10 alone. The first red contact scores 4 with your cue ball, 3 with the opponent ball. Your cue knocking pins transfers the score; a separate foul adds 2. Opening-shot points go to the opponent. Alternate shots. Target: 60.

Eight practice positions with caroms requiring zero to three cushions. Successful shots advance the position in match play. Use Next artistic position to browse in practice. These are original exercises, not the official artistic competition program.

Clear your solids or stripes, then call and pot the eight. Groups are assigned after the break. Potting the eight too early loses the game; an eight on a legal break is respotted. A foul gives ball in hand.

No call required. Groups are assigned after a normal shot pots only one colour. Black on the break: rerack, same breaker. A foul grants one free shot, then a normal visit; cue placement is in baulk. The free shot permits either group first. Target: clear your group and black.

Contact the lowest number first. A legal nine wins. The nine starts on the foot spot. After a legal break, a push-out suspends first-contact and rail requirements; the opponent chooses who plays next. Three consecutive fouls lose the rack.

Contact the lowest number; call the ball and pocket. The ten wins only when it was the last object ball at the start of a legal called shot. Otherwise, spot it. An uncalled pot gives the opponent a choice to play or pass back. Push-out and three-foul loss apply.

Call a ball and pocket, or play a safety. A successful call counts every object ball potted on that shot. Ordinary foul: −1; illegal opening break: −2. Three consecutive ordinary fouls: an extra −15 and a new break. Rerack fourteen balls with the apex empty. Target: 50.

Player 1 owns pocket 3; player 2 owns pocket 4: the two corners at the rack end. Only your pocket extends your visit. A foul costs one ball; an unpaid penalty is recovered from later pots. A scratch grants cue placement behind the head line. Target: 8.

Call the ball, the ordered cushion sequence and the pocket. No kicks, combinations or kisses count. A foul costs one ball. Break pots are respotted and retain the turn. Cue in hand behind the head line after a scratch. Target: 8.

Alternate reds (one point) and a nominated colour (two to seven points). Colours are respotted while reds remain and after the final red; then clear colours in ascending order. Fouls award at least four points. Cue ball in hand is restricted to the D. The higher score wins.

A cannon scores 2, a red pot 3, an opponent cue pot 2. An in-off scores 3 off red or 2 off the opponent. Red is respotted; the opponent cue stays off until their visit. In-hand placement is in the D. Fouls award 2. Target: 100.

After the coloured-ball break, any remaining ball can be the cue ball. Each legal pot scores 1, including the cue ball. A foul awards the opponent 1 and removes a penalty ball. Without a pot, the required cushion and centre-line sequence must be completed. Target: 8.

Always use the coloured cue ball. Potting it after contact scores 1, removes an object ball and grants placement anywhere. The next in-hand shot must pot an object ball: another in-off is a foul. A foul awards the opponent a penalty ball. Target: 8.

Short match distances are used, with player 1 taking the opening shot and fixed one-pocket sides. Artistic positions are original exercises. Pocket jaws and cloth are simulated profiles, not certified equipment templates. Snooker miss/free-ball adjudication, jump-over fouls and some frozen-ball situations remain simplified. The optional English baulk-crossing competition rule is not enabled. Pyramid penalty balls are selected automatically.

Kotlin port of Pooltool physics models by Evan Kiefl and contributors. Apache 2.0. Motion, cue strike, ball collisions and Han 2005 cushions. Atom2Universe adds Android controls, rules, procedural rooms, artwork and audio.

Goriziana: inner white pins 8, outer pins 2, red pin 10 or 30 alone. First red-ball contact: 6. A cushion before the opponent ball doubles the points. Own pins transfer points; other fouls add 2. Alternate shots. Target: 100.

Pot your group, then the eight. No ball or pocket call, including the eight. Groups are decided after the break. An eight on the break is respotted. Early eight or eight with a foul loses. Cue in hand after fouls; behind the head line after a break foul.

The short guide follows the cue ball for 3 m, then up to 90 cm for each ball after the first collision. Each ball has an extra allowance to show up to 1.2 m after its first cushion rebound. Each path ends at the next ball contact, second cushion, pocket or stopping point. Lines fade at their limit. Aiming assistance in the game menu lets you choose No guide or Full simulation.

Arcade: set your aim, power and spin, then tap Ready. Stop the moving cursor in the green zone. A perfect timing picks the best evaluated shot close to your aim; a good timing allows smaller corrections. Outside the target zone, your original shot is played. Your target and calls are preserved. Push-outs and safeties keep your exact shot.
Stop the cursor in the green zone for the best local correction. Power is already set.
